headline: Lead Platform Engineer
profile: I lead platform engineering at a small London fintech, reporting to the CEO. I joined in 2023 to run IT and operations, grew the role into platform engineering, and now own architecture, infrastructure, identity and security, and carry production. I build the developer platform the team ships with and hold AI-written code to the same standard as anyone's: a written spec first, tests first, gated by CI and reviewed by a model from a second vendor.

experience.title: Lead Platform Engineer
bullets: Founded and run the internal developer platform for AI-assisted delivery, built around a golden path from spec to merge: a Claude Code plugin and an engineering-standards baseline rolled out to about 26 repositories by automated pull request, with new repositories brought under golden-path governance as code. Specs before code, tests first, a gate that stops an agent finishing until typecheck, lint and tests pass, and adversarial review by a second vendor's model, which is also how I review the team's work. Three colleagues now extend it (40+ of their pull requests merged since July 2026).
One of four engineers on the company's AI assistant product, now in pre-launch: scaffolded it (Next.js on Cloudflare Workers) and built its security baseline and its safety escalation to a person.

Wrote the product's release pack: a timed database restore drill (recovered in 2 min 15 s with no data lost), a rehearsed production rollback and de-duplicated on-call alerting. Diagnosed a public-site outage caused by an origin certificate that could not renew, and moved the domain to edge-served routing so it cannot recur.

Built the first version of the company's identity provider: WebAuthn passkeys on did:web with W3C Verifiable Credentials, the sign-in for internal applications since May 2026, with client libraries published on npm. Handed it over to a colleague in August 2026.

Run cloud and SaaS infrastructure as code through Terraform Cloud (plan on pull request, apply on merge, daily drift detection) across GitHub, Cloudflare, Kafka, Databricks and observability. Moved all hosting to Cloudflare Workers and retired Vercel (Sep 2026); removing Vercel's per-seat charges cut the monthly hosting bill roughly tenfold.

Put Microsoft 365 and access security under code: phishing-resistant MFA for admins, a geo-fenced sign-in policy piloted in report-only mode before enforcement, a scheduled quarterly compliance evidence pack, and leaver tooling that suspends access in every system and verifies nothing survives. Moved AWS from root-account use to IAM Identity Center.

Built an on-premises Python speech pipeline on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (NeMo transcription, diarisation, voiceprint speaker naming) for audio that cannot leave the building; it feeds searchable, human-verified records for decision and action tracking.

Building the Software Factory, an agent execution and evaluation platform with the same golden path as its backbone: sandboxed runs with per-run credentials, durable queue-driven dispatch, review stations against written criteria and an automatic revert watcher. Running in staging; no production runs yet.

Set technical direction through architecture decision records (44 of the company's 61) and wrote the onboarding guides and handovers colleagues work from. 1,400+ merged pull requests across 40 repositories in ten months, including agent-assisted work.

experience.title: Software development and retraining
bullets: Built Altimist's first website and launch waitlist on the Internet Computer in Motoko, which led to joining the company. Delivered a paid client website while retraining in full-stack development (JavaScript, React, Python, REST APIs, SQL). Tutored A-Level and IB mathematics privately.

experience.title: Teacher of Mathematics
bullets: Taught mathematics across Key Stages 3–5, including GCSE and A-Level, adapting lessons to gaps in pupils' understanding. Completed the NQT induction year and a further year.

earlier: Earlier: academic tutor and mentor, Leading Lights Tuition (2015–2018); special projects coordinator and volunteer corps member, City Year UK (2014–2016).
